openQuestions: Partial breadth pass: 82 cards/132 generation or family records inventoried; 126 raw entities counted. Priority review covered Charger, Challenger, Durango, Hornet, Viper, Journey, Caravan, Ram, Rampage and Attitude.
Viper five unknown statuses changed to ended on explicit OEM factory-closure evidence; only final VX I end is set to 2017. Earlier calendar generation boundaries remain null.
New-generation Charger status uses explicit Windsor production-launch evidence, not just European orders; 2026 European manufacturer press material corroborates present availability.
Temporary factory shutdowns do not by themselves establish a nameplate production end. October-2026 Windsor downtime reports were encountered; no generation end inferred.
Charger 2024 generation record combines BEV and later SIXPACK launches; powertrain/body stages need separate scoping before technical enrichment.

Durango III and Hornet remain unknown in this pass: contemporary lineup evidence was found, but a sufficiently precise 2026 factory-production/cessation reconciliation was not completed. Do not infer Durango end from obsolete Last Call announcements.
Dodge 1900 corporate founding versus first Dodge-branded car in 1914 are different events; no make-year change applied.
Original Challenger convertible body coverage merits verification; no body addition based on recollection.
Dodge Ram versus independent Ram brand and Dodge Rampage versus modern Ram Rampage must remain separated.
Attitude and newer Mexico-market Journey require GAC-brand production versus Dodge commercial periods to be reconciled.
Historic manufacturer dates, all raw entity duplicates/non-cars, generation codes, photos and technical rows remain incomplete.

Depth6 partial: Caliber three existing engine/fuel/drive/transmission-type rows independently corroborated. Weight/performance retain OEM-only support; later2.2CRD/SRT4 and remaining81 Dodge lines need depth.
summary: Partial Dodge sweep replaced unknown status on five ended Viper generations, set final Viper end to 2017 from explicit OEM factory-closure evidence, and confirmed current new Charger production.
